title: Plan for Oswald to fire a deliberate miss at the motorcade and blame Cuba
summary: Dan Sheehan tells of Plan for Oswald to fire a deliberate miss at the motorcade and blame Cuba, about 1963 at Dealey Plaza, Dallas, and summarises it without a named source. As told, not a fact.

tellings.quote: what what the the plan was is to coax him into taking a shot at the motorcade, not hitting anybody, but taking a shot at the motorcade.

related.note: Both tell Sheehan's account of the plan for Oswald's shot and Tippit's role. Here Oswald shoots at Kennedy, while the story has a deliberate miss to blame Cuba.

plain: Dan Sheehan, a lawyer and researcher, says on Jesse Michels' podcast that the plan in Dallas in 1963 was to coax Lee Harvey Oswald, the man accused of killing President Kennedy, into firing at the president's motorcade on purpose without hitting anyone. According to Sheehan, the shot was meant to be blamed on Cuba, which would have given a reason to move against that country, and he ties the story to J. D. Tippit, a Dallas police officer killed that same day.
